territorial_scope.description: Applies to online undertakings regardless of national origin whose operators meet the revenue threshold and are not affiliated with a licensee, reaching foreign online services.

evidence.quote: regardless of their national origin

summary.short: The CRTC sets base contribution requirements for online undertakings that, alone or with their broadcasting ownership group, have $25 million in annual contributions revenues and are not affiliated with a licensed broadcaster: 5% of those revenues to designated Canadian and Indigenous content funds from the 2024-2025 broadcast year.
summary.long: CRTC Broadcasting Regulatory Policy 2024-121 imposes base contribution requirements on online undertakings through proposed orders under the Broadcasting Act. They cover operators not affiliated with a licensee, where the operator, alone or with its broadcasting ownership group, has $25 million in annual contributions revenues, excluding audiobook, podcast, video game, user-generated content and exempt-undertaking revenue. Covered operators must devote at least 5% of the previous broadcast year's annual contributions revenues to Canadian and Indigenous content from the 2024-2025 broadcast year. Audio-visual operators allocate this among the Canada Media Fund (2%, with up to 1.5% reducible by certified Canadian content expenditures), the Independent Local News Fund (1.5%), the Indigenous Screen Office Fund (0.5%), diversity funds (0.5%) and eligible production funds (0.5%). Audio operators allocate it among FACTOR and Musicaction (2%), a temporary commercial radio news fund (1.5%), the Canadian Starmaker Fund and Fonds RadioStar (0.5%), the Community Radio Fund of Canada (0.5%), flexible initiatives (up to 0.35%) and an Indigenous music fund (0.15%). Operators file reviewed financial statements, and the Commission will publish aggregate contributions per fund.

notes: The base contribution conditions are proposed orders with comment periods ending 14, 25 June and 2 July 2024. The text does not show they were made, so the registry status in_force applies to the policy document, not the orders. The text is inconsistent on the threshold: the summary and appendix use '$25 million or more' (and the appendix exceptions use 'less than $25 million'), while the Commission's decision uses 'more than $25 million'. On the audio sector IMO allocation, the decision says the remaining 0.10% 'should only be made once that fund is in operation', while the appendix says it 'shall be held until the Commission approves the fund'. Target instrument IDs are not in the text, so they are left empty and identified by target_text.

thresholds.value_text: more than $25 million in annual contributions revenues
thresholds.measurement: Annual contributions revenues (annual Canadian gross broadcasting revenues less excluded revenue) from the previous broadcast year, assessed for an online undertaking alone or for its broadcasting ownership group
thresholds.consequence: Online undertaking, alone or as part of a broadcasting ownership group, is required to make base contributions
thresholds.conditions: Operator not a licensee, not affiliated with a licensee, and not operating or affiliated with an exempt broadcasting undertaking requiring licensing. Summary wording reads '$25 million or more' while the operative wording reads 'more than $25 million'; the boundary at exactly $25 million is not resolved in the text.
